findings.note: The hand-maintained anchor list omits the one line the spec names first, and it is the line that carries exit 3. internal/fsm/cli/prompt.go:9 emits 'The loop: `advance` -> exit 3: do the node's work -> `record node-output` (the exact command is in `record`) -> `advance`.' (golden line 5). tests/go/agent-prompt-anchors.txt goes from line 1 (the re-entry sentence, prompt line 3) directly to line 2 ('exit 2: nothing was recorded...', prompt line 6): the loop-skeleton sentence in between has no anchor. docs/specs/2026-08-27-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-cli.md:229 lists it as the first required literal of the anchor list ('the loop skeleton: "`advance` -> exit 3: do the node's work -> `record node-output` ... -> `advance`"'), so this is a stated contract, not a preference. It matters because of what the anchor file is for: the golden is regenerated on demand with FSM_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 and tests/go/test-fsm.sh:63 only cmp's the regenerated bytes against themselves, so the anchor grep at tests/go/test-fsm.sh:66 is the sole invariant that survives a regeneration. Every other driver exit code is anchored (exit 2 at line 2, exit 1/GATE_FAILED at line 3, exit 1/ERR_* at line 4), leaving exit 3 -- the signal that the FSM needs the host to do a node's work, and the axis the whole driver contract turns on, documented in CLAUDE.md's exit handling -- as the only one that could be dropped from the shipped prompt with the suite still green. The count guard does not help: the file has 28 anchors against a floor of 20 at tests/go/test-fsm.sh:68, so eight lines can vanish before the count notices. Fix is one line appended to tests/go/agent-prompt-anchors.txt.

(a) internal/fsm/mockai/mockai.go:97 guards 'tok.Negative() || tok.TooLarge()'; the only invalid-token fixture is internal/fsm/mockai/mockai_test.go:65 with 'input: -1', so deleting the TooLarge() half keeps every test green -- and TooLarge is the guard that stops a scenario from injecting counters above run.MaxTokenCounter (internal/fsm/run/types.go:115) into an audited run's token totals, which is exactly what a mock scenario is in a position to do. findings.note: go.mod's new comment claims 'go 1.26 ... is the oldest Go someone can install with' (go.mod:7) and INSTALL.md:9 repeats it as a prerequisite, but nothing in the repository ever builds at that floor and the toolchain line partly contradicts it. With toolchain go1.27.0 (go.mod:14), a user who actually has Go 1.26 gets a build only under the default GOTOOLCHAIN=auto, which downloads the 1.27.0 toolchain over the network; under GOTOOLCHAIN=local, an offline machine, or a restricted GOPROXY, 'go run ./cmd/metareview' -- the documented source-checkout fallback (INSTALL.md:34) and the npm launcher's fallback -- fails outright rather than building at the declared minimum. The same release adds the first external dependency (go.mod:16, gopkg.in/yaml.v3), so that fallback now also needs a module fetch where it previously needed only the stdlib; go.sum is shipped (package.json's files list gained it on this branch) so this is bounded to a download, not a checksum failure. CI cannot catch either: .github/workflows/test.yml:30 uses go-version-file: go.mod, which setup-go resolves to the toolchain line, so every job runs 1.27.0 and the 1.26 claim is asserted by comment only. Either add a floor build (GOTOOLCHAIN=local with go 1.26) or state the toolchain caveat where the prerequisite is documented.
